This is like 2 months late, but if you still want to learn how to draw I would suggest drawing from life. Get yourself a sketchpad and draw objects. Pay attention to little subtle detail such as shadows and curves; find out how things are designed. For humans, I used "The Structure Of Man" a video course that helped me with proportions and other things. You don't need to necessarily take his style or methods to heart, but it is one way of understanding the human body and how everything lines up.

As for materials, any pencil or canvas works, but if you shop around and find one that you are comfortable with the most, use it. Most importantly practice. Don't forget to innovate as well. By trying new things you can learn a lot as well. What works, what doesn't and where they can work. Mix things up a bit.
